svg.title: Shared-interleaver Hankel multiplier — complete folded optical circuit
svg.desc: Component-level schematic, not a mask layout. Blue A and teal B are separate comb bands. Balanced electro-optic Mach–Zehnder interferometers with two 3 dB couplers implement the mode switches. Their fourth ports are terminated. The two external reciprocal route switches connect each band to its source or to a common read output. Band B always crosses the same selected port pair of a balanced unbalanced-path interferometer with 20 ps differential delay. Two selected rail ends serve both directions of one six-stage interleaver. Its six balanced couplers precede differential common delays and whole-band B detours, followed by a separate balanced end coupler. At the guide end two reciprocal switches connect band A or B to the input bus of one waveguide that uses the Kerr nonlinearity for co-propagating four-wave mixing (FWM) or to the amplified return bus. Both inputs can use the FWM input bus during a write. Forward launches A, selects B after FWM and returns B to the external readout. Adjoint launches B, selects A after FWM and returns A. Write launches saved A and residual B, closes the old-weight tap, and directs the new coefficient band to a timed coherent injection coupler in the fiber loop. The reference is available in all three modes with mode-specific slot phase. The selected full raw read family reaches G1 before the return mesh. The final time gate precedes G2. G1 and G2 are read amplifiers only. Unselected operand bands are suppressed at blocking gates; the CW reference is dumped. A tunable directional tap takes a fraction of the circulating weights on reads and is set to zero extraction for the write. Its insertion loss and the injection through-port loss are part of loop compensation. The long TTT weight loop includes one in-line section of dispersion-compensating fiber shared by all 127 weight teeth before the read tap and coherent write coupler on their next visit. The load or write selector, coherent scaling and phase trim, coupled injection, loop stabilization, and unused ports are shown. Reciprocal switches and band devices are a proposed realization of the end routers; their excess loss, spectral phase, gain and memory retention require a physical budget. Physical band centers and component dimensions are unspecified.

g.title: Six-stage reciprocal interleaver and fixed 50:50 end coupler
g.desc: Seven reciprocal balanced couplers connect two parallel rails. After each of the first six couplers, the upper rail is direct and the lower rail has a common delay spiral followed by a whole-band splitter, a blue A bypass and a teal B detour, and a whole-band recombiner. Base delays are 45, 90, 180, 360, 720 and 1440 ps. The corresponding additional B delays are 0.3125, 0.625, 1.25, 2.5, 5 and 10 ps. All four end ports are shown. Physical lengths are schematic.

g.inkscape:label: Operation settings
g.text: Set each port MZI for the selected pass.
Forward gate opens at 63P + T. Adjoint gate opens at 63P.
Launch the B residual 19.6875 ps ahead of the weight frame.
Optical paths are schematic. End-router loss, broadband phase response and memory-loop gain are open design parameters.
T = 20 ps · P = 45 ps · 64-slot frame = 2.88 ns
